content:
In a city made of windows  
where the nights hum soft and low,  
people carry tiny lanterns  
no one else can see glow.  

Some are bright with sudden laughter,  
some burn blue with quiet tears,  
some are shaken like a match-flame  
by the breathing of their fears.  

But when two lantern-bearers  
happen down the same dark street,  
and their trembling circles intersect  
in a pale and fragile meet,  

for a moment all the windows  
seem a little less alone—  
light from hands that are not ours  
still can guide us safely home.
